notes.short: God's regret and grief, told in human words
notes.about: Scripture tells of the LORD's regret and grief in human words, so that we can understand how God regards man's sin. The same Bible says He “is not a man, that He should change His mind” (1 Samuel 15:29).

figure.name: Anthropopatheia
figure.means: how God regards man's sin, told in human words

original.note: “Regretted” is nacham, the word Numbers 23:19 and 1 Samuel 15:29 use when they say God does not “change His mind”.

notes.evidence: Bullinger lists Genesis 6:6 under Anthropopatheia, human feelings spoken of God. Gill calls it speaking after the manner of men, yet says there can be no uneasiness in God's mind; Keil and Delitzsch see the pain of the divine love; Wesley and Jamieson, Fausset and Brown also read it as said after the manner of men. Numbers 23:19 and 1 Samuel 15:29 say God does not change His mind.
notes.limit: The writers agree the words are a figure, but not on whether they tell of a real grief in God or of His displeasure at sin and a change in how He deals with men.

cites.quote: not that He has such feelings; but, in infinite condescension, He is thus spoken of in order to enable us to comprehend Him.
cites.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

cites.quote: This is speaking by an anthropopathy, after the manner of men … there can, no more be any uneasiness in his mind than a change in it; for God is a simple Being, uncompounded, and not subject to any passions and affections.
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

cites.quote: The repentance of God is an anthropomorphic expression for the pain of the divine love at the sin of man
cites.read: sacred-texts.com's transcription, in the copy at github.com/jonnyg23/mahabrain (commit b00aa50)

cites.quote: These are expressions after the manner of men, and must be understood so as not to reflect upon God's immutability or felicity.
by language suited to our nature and experience, He is described as about to alter His visible procedure towards mankind
